claim: An unhealthy instance is one whose hardware has become impaired, or one that is not passing a user-configured ELB health check; EC2 Auto Scaling checks each instance at regular intervals and can also run ELB health checks when the instance is connected to a load balancer.
question: How does the AWS FAQ define an unhealthy instance in EC2 Auto Scaling?

values.display: hardware has become impaired
not passing a user-configured ELB health check

evidence.quote: An unhealthy instance is one where the hardware has become impaired for some reason (bad disk, etc.), or it is not passing a user-configured ELB health check. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling performs health checks on each individual EC2 instance at regular intervals, and if the instance is connected to an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer, it can also perform ELB health checks.

note: FAQ quick-fire; demand d75 (unhealthy instance) and d19.

claim: The SetInstanceHealth API lets you mark an instance UNHEALTHY yourself, which results in its termination and replacement; this is how a custom health check reports to the group.

result in a termination and replacement

note: FAQ quick-fire: Can I customize a health check?

ResumeProcesses

evidence.quote: Yes, you can temporarily suspend Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling health checks by using the SuspendProcesses API. You can use the ResumeProcesses API to resume automatic health checks.

claim: If the group uses Elastic Load Balancing, select the ELB health check; if it does not, select the EC2 health check.

select the EC2 health check

evidence.quote: If you are using Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) with your group, you should select an ELB health check. If you’re not using ELB with your group, you should select the EC2 health check.

claim: You do not have to use ELB to use Auto Scaling: the EC2 health check can identify and replace unhealthy instances on its own.

values.display: don't have to use ELB to use Auto Scaling
EC2 health check to identify and replace unhealthy instances

question: Do ELB health checks in EC2 Auto Scaling work with Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers?

values.display: works with Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers including their health check feature

evidence.quote: Yes, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling works with Application Load Balancers and Network Load Balancers including their health check feature.

claim: EC2 Auto Scaling does not automatically add a volume when an existing volume approaches capacity; a volume is attached to a new instance when that instance is added, and the EC2 API adds a volume to an existing instance.
question: Can EC2 Auto Scaling add storage to an instance without adding an instance?

values.display: doesn't automatically add a volume when the existing one is approaching capacity

evidence.quote: A volume is attached to a new instance when it is added. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling doesn't automatically add a volume when the existing one is approaching capacity. You can use the EC2 API to add a volume to an existing instance.

note: FAQ quick-fire: scaling adds instances, not storage.

claim: A stateful instance holds data that exists only on that instance, so terminating it loses that data; use lifecycle hooks to copy the data off before termination, or enable instance protection so EC2 Auto Scaling does not terminate it.
question: What is a stateful instance, and what does the FAQ suggest to avoid losing its data on scale-in?

values.display: exists only on that instance
lifecycle hooks to copy the data off
enable instance protection

evidence.quote: When we refer to a stateful instance, we mean an instance that has data on it, which exists only on that instance. In general, terminating a stateful instance means that the data (or state information) on the instance is lost.

You may want to consider using lifecycle hooks to copy the data off of a stateful instance before it’s terminated, or enable instance protection to prevent Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling from terminating it.

claim: When an impaired instance fails a health check, EC2 Auto Scaling automatically terminates it and replaces it with a new one; with an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer it detaches the impaired instance from the load balancer before provisioning the replacement.
question: Who replaces a failed instance in a group behind a load balancer, and in what order does detach and replace happen?

values.display: automatically terminates it and replaces it with a new one
gracefully detaches the impaired instance from the load balancer before provisioning a new one

evidence.quote: When an impaired instance fails a health check, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically terminates it and replaces it with a new one. If you’re using an Elastic Load Balancing load balancer, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling gracefully detaches the impaired instance from the load balancer before provisioning a new one and attaching it to the load balancer.

note: FAQ quick-fire; demand d21 (the load balancer does not replace instances; Auto Scaling does).

claim: A termination policy decides which instances EC2 Auto Scaling terminates first when it scales in; instance protection prevents EC2 Auto Scaling from selecting specific instances for termination when scaling in.
question: How do you control which instances are terminated on scale-in, and how do you exempt one instance?

values.display: termination policy
instance protection to prevent Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling from selecting specific instances for termination when scaling in

evidence.quote: When you have Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling automatically scale in, you must decide which instances Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling should terminate first. You can configure this through the use of a termination policy. You can also use instance protection to prevent Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling from selecting specific instances for termination when scaling in.

claim: If data on an instance must survive scale-in, store it off the instance in a service such as S3, RDS or DynamoDB.
question: Where does the FAQ say to keep data that must survive the termination of an Auto Scaling instance?

values.display: S3, RDS, or DynamoDB
stored off the instance

evidence.quote: If you have data on an instance, and you need that data to be persistent even if your instance is scaled in, then you can use a service like S3, RDS, or DynamoDB, to make sure that it is stored off the instance.

claim: Replacing an unhealthy instance with a new InService instance takes minutes: most replacements happen in less than 5 minutes, and the time depends on factors such as how long the AMI takes to boot.

values.display: less than 5 minutes
within minutes

qualifiers.condition: depends on factors such as AMI boot time

evidence.quote: The turnaround time is within minutes. The majority of replacements happen within less than 5 minutes, and on average it is significantly less than 5 minutes. It depends on a variety of factors, including how long it takes to boot up the AMI of your instance.

claim: When ELB notices that an instance is unhealthy it stops routing requests to it, but requests sent to that instance before the problem is discovered fail; they are not queued for other instances.

your own reverse proxy
service discovery solutions

claim: EC2 Auto Scaling integrates with IAM, and its resource-level permissions can restrict access to a particular Auto Scaling group or launch configuration.

values.display: resource-level permissions
restrict access to a particular EC2 Auto Scaling group or launch configuration

claim: If the AMI contains a CloudWatch agent, the agent is present on the instances the group launches; with the stock Amazon Linux AMI you need to install it yourself.

claim: A single Auto Scaling group can provision and scale EC2 capacity across different instance types, Availability Zones, and On-Demand, RI and Spot purchase options, with a chosen split between On-Demand and Spot capacity.

values.display: On-Demand, RIs and Spot purchase options in a single Auto Scaling Group
desired split between On-Demand and Spot capacity

You can provision and automatically scale EC2 capacity across different EC2 instance types, Availability Zones, and On-Demand, RIs and Spot purchase options in a single Auto Scaling Group. You have the option to define the desired split between On-Demand and Spot capacity, select which instance types work for your application, and specify preference for how EC2 Auto Scaling should distribute the ASG capacity within each purchasing model.

claim: A group can be configured so that all of its capacity is only Spot Instances, or all of its capacity is only On-Demand Instances and RIs.
question: Can an Auto Scaling group be all Spot, or all On-Demand and Reserved?

values.display: all capacity to be only Spot instances
all capacity to be only On-Demand instances and RIs

evidence.quote: Yes. You can configure your ASG specifying all capacity to be only Spot instances or all capacity to be only On-Demand instances and RIs.

claim: When combining purchase models, you can set the group's base capacity to be fulfilled by On-Demand Instances; as the group scales, anything beyond the base is fulfilled with only Spot Instances or with a specified percentage mix of On-Demand and Spot.
question: How does a mixed-instances group keep a base of On-Demand capacity and scale out on Spot?

values.display: base capacity be fulfilled with On-Demand instances
specified percentage mix of On-Demand or Spot instances

evidence.quote: Yes. When setting up an ASG to combine purchasing models, you can specify the base capacity of the group to be fulfilled by On-Demand instances.

As the ASG scales in or scale out, EC2 Auto Scaling ensures the base capacity be fulfilled with On-Demand instances and anything beyond that be fulfilled with either only Spot instances or a specified percentage mix of On-Demand or Spot instances.

note: FAQ quick-fire; demand d52 and d54.

claim: An existing group can be updated to change its mixed-instances settings: instance types, the prioritization order for On-Demand Instances, the percentage split between On-Demand and Spot, and the allocation strategy.
question: Can the purchase-option mix and instance types of an existing Auto Scaling group be changed after creation?

percentage split between On-Demand and Spot instances, and allocation strategy

claim: Reserved Instance discounts apply to On-Demand Instances that a group launches: if you hold RIs for an instance family and EC2 Auto Scaling launches a matching instance, you receive RI pricing.

claim: A group can use any instance type available in the Region, and each instance type can carry an optional weight that defines how many capacity units an instance of that type contributes.

claim: If none of the specified instance types are available in an Availability Zone, Auto Scaling retargets the launches to the group's other Availability Zones; it always prefers to keep compute balanced across zones.

always prefer keeping your compute balanced across Availability Zones
